bugs.title: checklist_get reports 6/6 done for B-3f3d while findings F-118 and F-119 prove CHK-005 and CHK-004 never delivered their declared userSees output. CHK-005 promises five labeled literal lines but review-inventory-epoch-smoke.ts:782 prints JSON and throws an uncaught AssertionError instead of printing FAIL; CHK-004 promises literal strings including 'Remediation authorized once by epoch <id>' and 'This receipt does not authorize TEST' which have zero grep hits anywhere in packages/main/src. This is the same class of misleading-green signal as BUG-VERIFIED-COUNT-MISREADS-AS-CLEAN and BUG-STATUS-STALE-LANE.

bugs.title: review_inventory epoch writes serialize on a single per-story lock (.lattice/locks/review-inventory/<story>-epochs.lock), so parallel reviewer lanes contend for it on every review_run_start and review_pass_set. Observed on B-3f3d RI-048: quality waited ~7min, test-coverage ~6min, and in wave 2 the docs lane was starved through 45+ consecutive failed attempts (RR-482..RR-533) until the competing writer stopped, nearly losing ~40min of completed review work. Each failed attempt also burns a ReviewRun id. Wait time grows with dispatch parallelism, so the documented parallel-lane workflow degrades exactly as it scales. Contention is worsened by any concurrent status polling, which takes the same lock. Consider finer-grained locking (per-lane rows), a queue with fair ordering, or making review_pass_set retry internally rather than surfacing lock timeout to the caller.

evidence.symptom: Parallel reviewer lanes contend on a single per-story inventory lock
reproSteps: Observe lock timeouts and burned ReviewRun ids
evidence.rootCause: Epoch writes serialize on one story-wide lock
evidence.fixEvidence: Filed as B-3f3d-FOLLOWUP-STORIES.md. Lock granularity is a follow-up; this story delivered saturation gating, not a lock redesign.

bugs.title: Three separate checklist items on this story declared userSees output that no code path produces: CHK-003 (F-120: promises 'Wave: n/max' and lane states pending|complete|blocked, but review-inventory.ts:258 emits 'Current wave: n/max' and the ReviewInventoryLaneTerminal type at types.ts:1670 is only 'pass'|'finding'), CHK-004 (F-119) and CHK-005 (F-118). All three were marked done and all three passed DEV-to-REVIEW. Each was caught only by a human-style reviewer grepping for the promised literals, and only across three separate waves -- wave 1 caught none, wave 2 caught two, wave 3 caught the third. Nothing in the pipeline compares a userSees string against emitted output, so the field carries the weight of a delivery contract while receiving none of the enforcement. Either mechanically check declared literals against code, or stop presenting userSees as a contract.

bugs.title: currentTopologyReceiptStateForContext (proofstory.ts:309) verifies preReview?.preReviewBasisArtifact ?? planArtifact and throws at line 323 when basisVerification fails, BEFORE either verdict branch, so topology_critic_receipt_set is closed for BOTH pass and request_changes. Preferring the frozen pre-review snapshot is correct security design -- it is captured at pre-review time (pre-review-check.ts:366) so the story owner cannot regenerate their way past the critic. The defect is that once that snapshot goes stale (here: scope-contract changed Aug 17, snapshot dated Aug 16), the only writer that can refresh it is pre_review_check, which is allowedPhases ['DEV'], and DEV requires a finalized review-inventory receipt, which requires a critic terminal state, which is exactly what is blocked. Regenerating the plan basis does not help because line 309 ignores it whenever a pre-review artifact exists. Verified live: topology_critic_receipt_set with verdict=request_changes throws identically to verdict=pass; an independent topology-critic agent reproduced this on its own dispatch. A critic must be able to record request_changes even when the basis it is judging is stale -- refusing a NEGATIVE verdict on stale evidence is what makes the deadlock inescapable.

evidence.symptom: topology_critic_receipt_set threw for both pass and request_changes once the pre-review snapshot went stale
reproSteps: Call topology_critic_receipt_set with verdict=request_changes after scope-contract moved
Observe basisVerification throw before either verdict branch
evidence.rootCause: currentTopologyReceiptStateForContext verified the frozen pre-review snapshot unconditionally and threw before the verdict split
evidence.fixEvidence: Commit 9f9f53a514 moved the stale-basis requirement onto the pass branch so request_changes can be recorded. Follow-up tests remain documented in B-3f3d-FOLLOWUP-STORIES.md Story A.

bugs.title: deriveRoleProvenance (topology-critic-receipt.ts:139-158) requires a recorded dispatch process-event whose sessionId EQUALS the signing session's own id, plus matching storyId, businessCommit and storyFilesHash. But 'dispatch' is not in the topology critic's allowedCommandIds (prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:300 lists only topology_critic_receipt_set, topology_critic_receipt_check, review_run_start, finding_add, review_pass_set, review_inventory_critic_set), so the critic cannot record the dispatch event it needs. A dispatch issued by the orchestrating agent records that agent's sessionId, which never matches the freshly-spawned subagent's session, so it does not satisfy the check either. Verified live: two independently dispatched critic sessions both failed with 'no current registered dispatch provenance for lattice-review-topology-critic in session sess-710f...' on BOTH verdicts, while review_run_start from the same sessions succeeded. Result: topology_critic_receipt_set is unreachable for any correctly-sandboxed critic subagent, independently of the basis-verification deadlock already fixed in 9f9f53a514. Either the host must inject dispatch provenance into the subagent session, or dispatch must be recordable by the critic role, or the binding must key on something the critic can actually present.

evidence.symptom: Sandboxed critic cannot record the dispatch event deriveRoleProvenance requires
evidence.rootCause: dispatch is not in critic allowedCommandIds and orchestrator dispatch uses a different session id
evidence.fixEvidence: Durable signing path is B-49ed SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES host-adapter|generated-token, already DONE on local main. Residual design follow-up remains in B-3f3d-FOLLOWUP-STORIES.md Story A.

bugs.title: independenceMatrix (topology-critic-receipt.ts:181-188) establishes independence by four textual !== comparisons (agentId, sessionId, dispatchId, businessCommitAuthor) between the critic and the implementation provenance. Neither deriveRoleProvenance (139-179) nor deriveImplementationProvenance (119-137) verifies WHO originated or recorded a dispatch event; both simply read sessionId off the most recent matching ProcessEvent on disk. Consequence: an implementer who also dispatches can mint a session id, record a dispatch event under it, hand that id to the critic subagent via the documented LATTICE_SESSION_ID host-adapter override, and the matrix reports session independence as true while the implementer controlled both sides of the comparison. I attempted exactly this and an independent topology critic refused to adopt the supplied session, correctly identifying that the proxy is void when one party originates both identities. Verified live: the dispatch event recorded under an arbitrary implementer-chosen session id carried a valid headHash and businessCommitAuthorSource git-var:GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT, i.e. it satisfies every mechanical check. The mechanism cannot catch this class of bypass; only the reviewer refusing at the point of session adoption catches it. Either bind identity to something the implementer cannot mint, or document that critic independence rests on reviewer refusal rather than on the matrix.

evidence.symptom: independenceMatrix compares textual ids an implementer can mint
reproSteps: Hand the id to a critic via LATTICE_SESSION_ID
evidence.rootCause: Matrix uses !== on agentId/sessionId/dispatchId/author without origin verification
evidence.fixEvidence: Filed as B-3f3d-FOLLOWUP-STORIES.md Story A. Host-adapter signing from B-49ed is the mechanical independence floor; remaining matrix hardening is follow-up.

bugs.title: REVIEW to TEST validates the Prompt Envelope of findings that are already RESOLVED, and no command can repair a stale envelope. On B-3f3d the gate refuses with review_evidence_invalid naming F-088 through F-092 for eligibilityDigest/changedFilesDigest/impactedFilesDigest/reviewBasisDigest mismatch against authoritative recomputation; four of those five (F-088, F-090, F-091, F-092) are status=resolved and only F-089 is open, yet all five still block. Envelopes are written at dispatch/review_run time (handlers/story-dispatch.ts, handlers/review-run.ts) and bound to the material state then current, so a later material change staleifies them permanently. verification_evidence_refresh_stale does not touch them and timed out at 300s here; no envelope-specific repair command exists in the CLI surface. The only apparent recovery is a fresh reviewer round that mints new envelopes, which for a topology-critic-lane finding such as F-089 interacts with BUG-CRITIC-FINDINGS-INVISIBLE. Either resolved findings should be exempt from envelope validation, or a repair path should exist.

evidence.symptom: REVIEW to TEST validates Prompt Envelopes of already-resolved findings with no repair command
reproSteps: Advance TEST and observe review_evidence_invalid on resolved ids
evidence.rootCause: Envelopes bind to dispatch-time material and have no refresh path
evidence.fixEvidence: This story recovered by minting fresh current-round reviewer receipts. Envelope repair/exempt-resolved is a follow-up filed as BUG-PROMPT-ENVELOPE-UNREPAIRABLE.

bugs.title: B-3f3d's three remaining open findings (F-113, F-117, F-121, all high, all from lattice-review-topology-critic) cannot be cleared inside this worktree, and the reason is now mechanically established rather than inferred. F-113 and F-117 report that topology_critic_receipt_set threw for both verdicts; that specific cause was fixed here in commit 9f9f53a514, which moved the basis requirement off an unconditional throw onto the pass branch. F-121 reports 'no current registered dispatch provenance'. Running lattice dispatch does NOT clear it: every dispatch event is keyed to the session that RAN the command, and inspection of process-events.jsonl shows the critic-lane events belong to sess-60b0d01c (mine), sess-db9d3c15, sess-f1ed9b22 and one hand-set sess-critic-b3f3d, while deriveRoleProvenance matches on the SIGNING session's own id. A freshly spawned critic subagent always has a different session id, so the match can never succeed. That is BUG-CRITIC-DISPATCH-PROVENANCE-UNSATISFIABLE, and the fix for it lives in story B-49ed (requiring sessionSource host-adapter, so a host-derived session satisfies provenance without the implementer minting it). Verified that B-49ed's guard is absent from this worktree: grep for SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES in packages/main/src/core/topology-critic-receipt.ts returns nothing here. So these three findings are blocked on B-49ed merging, not on further work in B-3f3d.

evidence.symptom: Three critic findings could not be cleared because topology_critic_receipt_set demanded a dispatch event in the signing session
reproSteps: Observe no current registered dispatch provenance
evidence.rootCause: deriveRoleProvenance required a same-session dispatch event that a sandboxed critic cannot record
evidence.fixEvidence: B-49ed is DONE on local main with SIGNABLE_SESSION_SOURCES host-adapter|generated-token. B-3f3d finding_list openCount=0 (F-113/F-117/F-121 resolved). Remaining critic-receipt design follow-ups live in B-3f3d-FOLLOWUP-STORIES.md Story A.
